Theorem
[Nonabelian fundamental group] 1. ch12:3.8If $M$ is compact and $K<0$, then $\pi _1(M)$ is not abelian.
Proof

\sketch Suppose $\pi _1(M)$ were abelian. If it were trivial, every geodesic in $\tilde M$ would be invariant under all deck transformations, contradicting item 2. Otherwise, choose a nonidentity deck transformation and its unique invariant geodesic. By item 2, every deck transformation preserves that geodesic, again contradicting item 2 and compactness.

□
